issues.claim: KEYENCE row pricing/spec entry: '20-megapixel sensor, up to 300 features per placement, optional rotary fixture'
issues.problem: Numbers are correct but the cited source_url is the IM-8000 get-pricing page, which is a registration wall and contains no specifications. The specs live on the product page.
issues.fix: Add https://www.keyence.com/products/measure-sys/image-measure/im-8000/ as the spec source and keep the get-pricing URL only as evidence of the sign-in wall.

issues.claim: Cognex In-Sight 2800 '...configured in the EasyBuilder interface and typically set up by an integrator'
issues.problem: 'Typically set up by an integrator' is not stated in the datasheet; it is an unsourced inference presented inside a vendor-description field.
issues.fix: Mark it '(inference)' or delete the clause; EasyBuilder, 1.6 MP and the five-to-ten-image training claim are supported.

issues.claim: MVTec HALCON row: 'calibrated metrology, blob/shape matching, plus deep-learning anomaly detection and classification operators'
issues.problem: The cited page (editions/licensing) covers only editions, evaluation length and the absence of published prices; it does not document the listed capabilities.
issues.fix: Cite a HALCON product/feature page for the capability description, or trim the description to what the licensing page supports.

issues.claim: Landing AI row: 'downloadable ONNX models deployed on edge devices'
issues.problem: The LandingLens plans page documents LandingEdge, a Docker app and model download limits, but does not mention ONNX export.
issues.fix: Say 'downloaded models deployed with LandingEdge' or cite a LandingEdge/export doc that names ONNX.

issues.claim: Problem summary: 'an inspector ... costs roughly $46-51k a year in this region'
issues.problem: The $51,160 figure is the New York-Newark-Jersey City metro mean; the ~$46k lower bound is the national median ($45,850), not a regional figure. The two numbers come from different geographies.
issues.fix: State 'about $51k mean in the NY-Newark-Jersey City metro, against a $45.9k national median' so the geography of each number is explicit.

issues.problem: Arithmetically consistent (13+8+13+10+15+8 = 67) and defensible because the design is video-only, bench-scoped and non-biometric, but 13 of a plausible 15-point weight is generous given the section records a state wiretap statute, a criminal hidden-camera provision and an unconfirmed notice duty.
issues.fix: Keep the score but add one sentence to the rationale noting that the score assumes the written design constraints (no audio, no face recognition, bench-only placement) are contractually enforced.

issues.problem: Unsourced assertion; the only cost source cited (Relling Systems) supports $15k-$60k single-camera stations and $150k+ multi-camera/3D builds, not integrator deal-size preference.
issues.fix: Label as inference, or anchor to the Relling figure ('stations above $60k are multi-camera/3D work').
